name: All Saints Academy - St. Rose Philippine Duchesne
historical_names: All Saints Academy - St. Rose Philippine Duchesne Campus
All Saints Academy - St. Rose Campus
district_operator: Archdiocese of St. Louis (All Saints Academy partnership)
notes: All Saints Academy was created January 2018 as a three-campus partnership school combining St. Ferdinand, St. Norbert, and St. Rose Philippine Duchesne parish schools in Florissant (first year 2018-19). The St. Rose Philippine Duchesne campus at 3500 St. Catherine St closed for the 2023-24 school year after enrollment fell from 238 to 131 students with $878k+ deferred maintenance; enrolled students were offered transfers to the academy's St. Ferdinand (ALL-014) or St. Norbert (ALL-013) campuses, so the successor is the academy continuing at those two campuses (both ids listed - no single successor). Predecessor parish school on this site: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne School (ALL-047 in batch03), formed 2005 from the merger of the St. Thomas the Apostle and St. Dismas elementary schools (flovalleynews.com/?p=13919). DATA-QUALITY FLAG: seed row ALL-108 'All Saints Academy - St. Rose Campus' in batch05 is the same entity under a duplicate row - coordinator should reconcile. The parish itself (St. Rose Philippine Duchesne, formed 2005) was merged into Sacred Heart Parish in August 2023 under All Things New.

name: St. Thomas the Apostle School
historical_names: St. Thomas the Apostle Catholic School
district_operator: St. Thomas the Apostle Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: SEED ADDRESS ERROR: seed lists '5300 Derby Lane' - no Derby Lane exists in Florissant; the parish and school were at 3500 St. Catherine St (Archdiocese closed-parishes list, St. Louis Genealogical Society, NCES-derived Education Bug listing all agree). Parish founded 1960 (formed from Our Lady of Fatima and St. Dismas territory); K-8 school documented at that address in NCES-derived records (~277 students). In the 2005 Northeast Deanery consolidation the parish was suppressed and merged with St. Dismas and part of Our Lady of Fatima to form St. Rose Philippine Duchesne Parish; per STLPR 'the school for the new parish will be at the current St. Thomas the Apostle School,' so the school entity continued as St. Rose Philippine Duchesne School (ALL-047 in batch03). Opening year not found online; school likely dates to the early-mid 1960s alongside the parish (founded 1960, church built 1966). Per St. Louis Review (Jan 2023), the current St. Rose school building previously housed Prep Seminary North, and 'the old St. Thomas School next door is now St. Catherine Retirement Community.'

name: St. Christopher School
district_operator: St. Christopher Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Parish school of St. Christopher Parish, Florissant (1967-2005), at 11755 Mehl Ave / 11575 Old Halls Ferry Rd; school documented in NCES-derived listings (Education Bug, Trulia) at that address. In the 2005 consolidation the parish was suppressed: territory north of I-270 joined St. Angela Merici Parish in Florissant (school = ALL-080, batch05; St. Angela Merici's own parish history confirms it 'welcomed its newest members from Transfiguration and St. Christopher' in July 2005), while territory south of I-270 merged with four other parishes into Holy Name of Jesus Parish, whose students attended the new Christ, Light of the Nations School at the former St. John Neumann site in Spanish Lake (itself closed 2020). So the school closed with its parish in 2005 (probable - closure documented at parish level, school disposition inferred) and students split between ALL-080 and Christ, Light of the Nations (not in dataset). The school's own opening year not found; likely mid-1960s-1970s alongside the parish (founded 1967). The site later housed a 'St. Christopher Learning Center' (Archdiocese special-education site; see ALL-056 notes).

name: Salem Lutheran School
notes: Corrected seed's 1895 (that is the one-room schoolhouse building date - see ALL-052). Per the congregation's own history: Salem Lutheran Church was organized November 1849 in New Bielefeld (now Black Jack), 'a school was organized soon after the church was established' with the pastor as teacher, and the first regular teacher (G. A. Just) was called in 1868 - 'school has been conducted without interruption to this day.' The founding year could be as early as ~1850; 1868 is the first firmly dated operation. Currently operating: re-enrollment open for 2026-27, PK-8, ~43 students (peak ~200 in the 2010s). Campus at 5180-5195 Parker Rd, Black Jack (mailing address Florissant 63033). Seed note about a 2026 all-school reunion is consistent with an active alumni association.

name: Salem Lutheran School - Original Building
historical_names: Salem Lutheran School Old School House
notes: BUILDING-VARIANT ROW, not a separate school: this is the 1895 one-room brick schoolhouse at ~5195 Parker Rd (St. Louis County Historic Buildings Inventory lists 'Salem Lutheran School, constructed c. 1895'). Per the church's own history it was built in 1895 across the street from the church and 'used as a classroom until 1950,' after which instruction continued in the school's newer facilities - so 'opened/closed' here are building-use dates for the same continuous school as ALL-051, which the seed deliberately split as an archival target. The 'Old School House' still stands, was designated a Historic Building of St. Louis County in 1970, and is used for youth group/Bible classes/applebutter canning. Note the county survey once incorrectly identified it as a public school. Kept as separate row per no-silent-merge rule; recommend coordinator treat as a campus of ALL-051.

name: Children's Village Christian School
notes: Operating per NCES-derived directory data (privateschoolreview 2026-27 profile): PK-3, ~4 students, 1 teacher, at 13505 New Halls Ferry Rd, Florissant. Founding year not findable via web sources - the school has essentially no independent web presence beyond directory listings. A very small early-childhood program; low likelihood of yearbook production. Related seed row ALL-059 ('Children's Village Christian School - Historical', another batch) appears to be a duplicate of this entity.

name: Gateway Legacy Christian Academy
notes: Founded 2005 (NCES-derived 'Year Founded 2005') by Greg and Melissa Morrison; grew from one classroom to two campuses enrolling international boarding students from 35+ countries. Seed address 1360 Grandview Dr, Florissant 63033 is the current MS/HS campus per the school's site. In 2019 GLCA acquired the former St. Stanislaus Seminary / Urshan College property at 700 Howdershell Rd, Hazelwood 63031 as its second campus (ribbon cutting Oct 3, 2019). FOX 2 reported (Feb 2023) that Florissant shut the school down from Dec 2022 over fire/safety code violations, with partial reoccupancy allowed after; the school continued operating - its admissions site is live and privateschoolreview lists a 2026-27 profile.

name: Faith Christian School
notes: Only stale business-directory listings found: schools-us.org lists 'Faith Christian School' and 'Faith Christian Schl & Academy' at 2300 Parker Road, Florissant 63033-2299 (principal Warren Stump / administrator Vincent Kobash, phone 314-837-5343) with undated 'Active' status. No NCES record, school website, news coverage, or founding/closure dates surfaced - the school may be defunct or may never have been more than a small church-school program. Related seed row ALL-143 ('Faith Christian School', ZIP 63042) is likely the same entity listed under a different ZIP. Recommended human follow-up: check Missouri DESE nonpublic school registrations or the church at 2300 Parker Rd.

name: Academy at St. Rose Philippine Duchesne
historical_names: The Academy at St. Rose Philippine Duchesne
district_operator: Archdiocese of St. Louis - Department of Special Education
notes: IDENTITY RESOLVED: this is NOT the All Saints Academy campus (ALL-048) - it is a distinct special-education school operated by the Archdiocese Department of Special Education at 1220 Paddock Dr, Florissant (NCES PSS record 00752221: ~33 students, ungraded/special education; principal Ms. Jay Persinger c. 2012). It was one of the archdiocese's 'The Academy at ...' satellite sites alongside the St. Christopher Learning Center and The Academy at St. Sabina. It does NOT appear on the 2017-18 archdiocese accredited-schools list, where the only Florissant special-ed entry is 'The Academy at St. Sabina' (1625 Swallow Ln) - suggesting the St. Rose site was consolidated into St. Sabina between ~2012 and 2017 (probable successor, not in dataset; note ALL-011 'St. Sabina School' is the parish elementary school, a different entity). CAUTION for other researchers: 'Academy of St. Louis' (private special-ed school founded ~2002-2004, now in Manchester) is similarly named but a different school entirely. Special-ed academies are unlikely yearbook producers.

name: Tendercare Learning Center
notes: Daycare/early-childhood center, not a K-12 school: 'Tendercare Learning Center #8' at 13775 New Halls Ferry Rd, Florissant holds an active Missouri DHSS child-care license (000566534, license holder Tendercare Academy Inc.), and tendercarelearningcenters.com lists an operating Florissant center. Note the address now also appears under the name 'Visionary Academy Prep' on childcarecenter.us - possible rebrand worth checking at archive-survey time. No yearbook value expected; retain for registry completeness only.

name: Alphabet Soup Learning Center
notes: Weak-attestation entity: LinkedIn shows a Florissant-based 'Alphabet Soup Learning Center' with a director listed Apr 1999-Oct 2005 and an owner listed Oct 2002-present, so a real early-childhood business by that name operated c. 1999-2000s. No address, NCES record, DHSS license, or current web presence found - likely closed or renamed. No yearbook value expected. Recommended human follow-up: Missouri DHSS child-care license history or Secretary of State business filings could confirm dates and address.

name: Hazelwood Central Middle School
notes: Resolved seed's unknown: new-construction school at 13450 Old Jamestown Road (Black Jack), dedication held April 18, 2007, opened for the 2007-08 school year as one of four middle schools built that year (with Hazelwood Southeast, North, and West middle schools) when the district moved 6th graders out of elementary schools into middle schools. Currently operating (district map + March 2026 district newsletter). No predecessor school occupied this site - see ALL-061 flag.

name: Hazelwood Central Middle School predecessor
notes: LIKELY PHANTOM ROW: no 'Central Junior High' or 'Central Intermediate School' ever existed in the Hazelwood School District per available sources. Documented Hazelwood junior highs were Kirby Junior High (in the first 1954 Hazelwood High building at 1865 Dunn Rd; renamed Kirby Middle in 2000 and Hazelwood East Middle in 2007 - see ALL-065) and Hazelwood Junior High/Middle (now Hazelwood Northwest Middle). Hazelwood Central Middle (ALL-060) was greenfield construction in 2007; its students were drawn by attendance-boundary redrawing and the 6th-grade shift from elementaries, not from a same-named predecessor. Retained per no-silent-deletion rule; recommend coordinator delete or fold into ALL-060's notes.

name: Hazelwood East High School
notes: SEED ERROR corrected: opened 1974, not 1965 - the school's own district page and Wikipedia both give 'Established 1974.' Classes of 1975-76 attended split sessions in the existing Hazelwood (Central) High building before the new facility at 11300 Dunn Rd (Spanish Lake, ZIP 63138 - seed's 63033 is attendance-zone metadata, not the address) opened fall 1976. Open-space classroom design; major renovation 2005. Currently operating (NCES CCD 2023-24, ~1,253 students). Yearbook: Pegasus; newspaper The Spartan Spectrum (of Hazelwood v. Kuhlmeier, 1988 Supreme Court fame). The Hazelwood East Middle School 8th Grade Center (ALL-065) shares the campus. Note related seed rows elsewhere: ALL-457 'Hazelwood East High School - Split Session 1974-1976' (batch16) documents the split-session period.

name: Hazelwood East Middle School
historical_names: Hazelwood East Middle School 8th Grade Center
notes: COMPLEX LINEAGE: the entity's building at 1865 Dunn Rd opened 1954 as the first Hazelwood High School; when the second Hazelwood High opened in 1966 (now Hazelwood Central High), the old building became Kirby Junior High (renamed Kirby Middle School in 2000, renamed Hazelwood East Middle School in 2007 when four new middle schools opened - flovalleynews 2011 corroborates 'formerly Kirby Junior High and the first Hazelwood High School building'). Seed address 11300 Dunn Rd reflects the ~2017-18 move INTO the Hazelwood East High campus as the thematic '8th Grade Center' (accelerated + traditional paths, high-school credit in 8th grade), opened under Superintendent Collins-Hart; the vacated 1865 Dunn building became the Hazelwood Opportunity Center (ALL-476, batch17). Opened_year 1966 = conversion of the old high school to Kirby JH (probable - exact conversion year inferred from Central HS's 1966 opening; schooldesigns.com describes the building's high-school-to-junior-high-to-middle-school history). Still operating: accepting 8th-grade applications for 2026-27 per the March 2026 district newsletter. Note duplicate seed rows ALL-088/ALL-127 in other batches are the same school listed under other ZIPs.
